result.title: When Bigger Becomes Brittle: Why Compression Hurts More as Language Models Scale
result.summary: Quantization and pruning reduce the cost of deploying language models, but their effects are usually reported as benchmark scores. Such scores record only the loss that remains at the output. Inside the model, compression damages some components more than others, and the rest of the network can partly compensate. The observed loss therefore reflects both the damage and this compensation, which benchmark scores cannot separate. How the two combine, and whether their balance changes with model size, remains unclear. We study this compensation for in-context retrieval, a capability carried by a small, identifiable set of attention heads. To separate the two, the expected loss from ablating these heads is decomposed exactly into the part restored by the rest of the network, attributed to the components responsible, and the part that reaches the output. This decomposition is then compared across model sizes. For damage of comparable size, smaller models restore most of the loss, whereas larger models retain most of it, because the compensating responses offset less of it as models grow. Compressing the heads produces the same pattern. Compression that is nearly harmless in small models can therefore be costly in large ones.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究量化与剪枝为何在模型变大时更伤性能：以 in-context retrieval 所依赖的一小群 attention heads 为例，把消融造成的期望损失精确分解为被网络其余部分恢复的部分（并归因到具体组件）与最终传导到输出的部分，再跨模型规模比较二者。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「损伤—补偿」精确分解与组件归因为分析 LVR 中答案是否真正使用 latent/视觉证据提供了可核查的线索：或可把被内部补偿掩盖的损伤与真正影响输出的损失分开，用于诊断视觉旁路与贡献分配，但迁移到多模态推理的有效性需核查。
